# Quantum Exclusion Noise Limits

Scientific question: how robust is exclusion of one of three known pure-qubit preparations, repeated under an unknown fixed label?

Start with README.md, science/README.md, then science/model.md. The ensemble is a fixed strict great-circle triple, and raw repetitions—not encoded codewords—are supplied. All joint POVMs are allowed in the converse.

Theorem route:
- science/adversarial.md: n >= 3t+1 is necessary and sufficient; local count decoder; coherent error-subspace adversary; symmetric-sector polynomial completeness obstruction.
- science/noise.md: explicit trace-norm coefficient functional, finite-n lower and upper risk bounds, fixed-n power ceil(n/3), and low-noise coefficient 1/3 for both liminf and limsup exponents.
- science/interpretation.md: resources, local versus collective distinctions, log-Euclidean comparison, orthogonal-pair boundary, and endpoints.

Attribution: references/RELATED_WORK.md and references/references.bib.
Reproduction: verification/README.md, verification/verify.py, verification/requirements.txt, verification/reference_results.json.

Do not replace the two asymptotic rates by an asserted fixed-noise limit. Do not call the local decoder exactly optimal at fixed noise. The constants depend on fixed geometry. No arbitrary-noise fault-tolerance or coding-capacity theorem is claimed. Learning route: learning/README.md gives a complete four-copy trine example. learning/MILESTONES.md has exactly M01--M30 (12 background, 18 narrative). learning/WATROUS_BRIDGE.md connects the selected single anchor, John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018), author standard-layout manuscript, to the project. Textbook foundations, locally supplied polynomial derivations, and research attribution are distinct. Personal learner records and coaching instructions do not belong here.
